summary: Alaska is a Metro Route-Based Social Network that connects commuters sharing similar daily routes on the Delhi Metro network. Users input their daily journeys, and the platform matches them using advanced algorithms (Suffix Automaton) to connect, add friends, and chat in real-time.

technicalDetails.architecture: Microservices Architecture utilizing Docker Compose. The system separates the core backend (Core API) from real-time features using a horizontally scaled Chat Gateway (for WebSockets) and Chat Worker (for DB persisting), all sitting behind an Nginx load balancer and a PgBouncer connection pooler.
technicalDetails.keyModules: 1. Core API (Handles business logic: users, trips, friendships, reviews). 2. Chat Gateway (Handles persistent WebSocket connections, assigns timestamps, and pushes to Redis streams). 3. Chat Worker (Pulls from Redis streams and performs batched bulk inserts into PostgreSQL). 4. Frontend (Handles UI, map rendering, and Suffix Automaton (SAM) generation).
technicalDetails.dataFlow: Client sends routes (SAM built on frontend) to Core API to match overlaps. Real-time chat flows from Client -> Nginx Load Balancer -> Chat Gateway (WebSocket) -> Redis Stream -> Chat Worker -> PostgreSQL. Messages are broadcast via Redis Pub/Sub to other Gateway replicas for cross-gateway delivery.
technicalDetails.setupAndConfiguration: Containerized via Docker. Dev environment is run via 'docker-compose up'. Env variables configure DB connection (using PgBouncer for multiplexing), Redis, and JWT secrets. Nginx routes traffic across multiple (5) replicas of chat-gateway and chat-worker. Daily cron jobs archive old trips.

strongPoints.justification: Separation of WebSocket holding (Chat Gateway) and database writing (Chat Worker) via a Redis Stream queue prevents DB bottlenecks. Horizontal scaling with Nginx and using consumer groups ensures messages aren't processed twice and aren't lost if a worker fails.
Frontend builds a Suffix Automaton (SAM) and maps strings to integers. This reduces matching to linear time (O(size(B))) on the backend and minimizes memory and string-comparison overhead.
Uses PgBouncer for connection pooling to multiplex requests from horizontally scaled microservices (Core API and 5 Chat Workers), preventing PostgreSQL connection exhaustion under high load.

uniquePoints: Utilizes Suffix Automaton (SAM) built on the client side for optimized substring matching of metro routes.
Decoupled message processing using Redis Streams to buffer spikes in chat traffic before batched inserts to PostgreSQL.
Maps 271 Delhi Metro station names to unique integers on the frontend to process arrays instead of strings over the wire.

fileAndFolderAnalysis.directoryStructureOverview: A monorepo-style structure containing separate directories for the backend API ('backend'), real-time WebSocket gateway ('chat-gateway'), queue consumers ('chat-worker'), and frontend code ('frontend'). Orchestrated by root Docker Compose configurations.

criticalFiles.purpose: Contains the core algorithm for deserializing the SAM and calculating overlapping routes (Longest Common Substring) for users.
Manages WebSocket events, enqueues incoming messages into Redis streams in memory-efficient batches.
Constantly polls the Redis Stream for new or stuck messages using consumer groups, and performs bulk inserts into PostgreSQL.
Orchestrates the entire microservices deployment including DB, Redis, PgBouncer, Nginx LB, API, and scaled chat services.

overallEvaluation: The project demonstrates excellent system design principles, explicitly focused on high availability and fault tolerance. By integrating advanced data structures (SAM) and robust patterns (Gateway-Worker-Queue, PgBouncer pooling), the architecture is highly scalable and maintainable. Code modularity is well-preserved across distinct microservices.
